newsitem.title: GREECE: UPDATED PRESS DIGEST - GREECE - OCT 8.
newsitem.headline: UPDATED PRESS DIGEST - GREECE - OCT 8.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek
press:
ELEFTHEROTYPIA
--Following the leadership scuffle in conservative opposition
party New Democracy, president Miltiades Evert denies rumours he
is only leader until the party convenes its congress. But
defeated leadership candidate George Souflias and his two
high-profile supporters keep the pressure on, saying they will
continue to work together within the party.
--Greek industries get hauled over the coals: They're
individualistic and centralised and expect too much from the
state, says senior economic analyst.
--Nicosia satisfied with Greek participation in military
exercise, in framework of Greek-Cypriot joint defence doctrine.
Turkish fighter jets violated Greek and Cypriot air space at
least 20 times yesterday. As long as there are occupation forces
on Cyprus, there will be a doctrine, Athens says.
TA NEA
--The fate of 2,850,000 social security fund contributors up in
the air. Seventeen of the 26 major funds face burgeoning
deficits and the inability to cover pension payouts from their
revenues, due to increased expenditures.
ETHNOS
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis puts the country on a strict
diet. The government's policy statements are ready to go and
went through a dress rehearsal at last night's meeting.
KATHIMERINI
--The government acknowledges that public spending is
uncontrolled and promises immediate cutback of 400 billion
drachmas.There are good margins for cutbacks in public
expenditures without compromising public services, Finance
Undersecretary Nikos Christodoulakis says.
--Tax checks to intensify: Finance Undersecretary George Drys
pressures tax officials to improve returns by the end of the
year.
-- New criteria hold sway for appointment to public utilities
(DEKO) and ministry positions. Open competitions to be held:
Defeated election candidates need not apply.
--Reduced profits and low turnover for three state-run casinos
so far this year.
IMERISIA
--Record forex inflow of 672 million dollars.
--Economy officials examining submitting two-year budgets which
would give the government the ability to distribute the burdens
of convergence over a longer period.
--Texaco, Shell and Aramco look at merging into a giant
petroleum retailer controlling 15 percent of the market.
--Government economic policy to gravitate on five axes for the
four-year period: reducing appointments to public sector,
activating returns from taxes, tapping funds for investment,
speedier procedures for completion of major public works
projects and increased subsidised job positions.
KERDOS
--Forecasts for the government's policy statements in
Parliament later this week - incentives for small and
medium-size enterprises and the stock market. Major
administrative changes across the the public sector board will
offset the effects of the restrictive economic policy the
government will follow in the coming year, Finance and Economy
Minister Yannos Papandoniou says.
--European Union gives the go-ahead for the reform of the
Skaramangas (Hellenic) Shipyards. Briefing on privatisation
procedure to be held tomorrow with EU official.
EXPRESS
--First target is credibility. The prime minister believes that
word and deed will cement the climate of consensus for the
convergence programme.
--Papandoniou promises fairer objective tax criteria but says
they will not be abolished just yet.
--Knife to fall on state procurements contracts, as part of
general cutback on state spending.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Outstanding tax debts over the past three years will not be
resettled, Finance Undersecretary George Drys tells tax
officials.
--Incomes policy for 1997 will be 'corrective'.
--Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
